kicker: Montevideo · Colonia del Sacramento · Punta del Este — Feb 5–13, 2027
title: Montevideo, Colonia del Sacramento, Punta del Este & Uruguay
dek: Nine days across Uruguay's capital, its UNESCO river town, and its Atlantic beach coast — dates that fall in the middle of the country's Carnival season.
verified: ⚠ Draft — checked 2026-08-23 for the Feb 5–13, 2027 trip, across an independent verification pass and a local/authenticity pass reconciled the same day. Confirmed against primary sources: entry rules for a US passport, the Carnival public holiday dates (Easter-relative, computed), intercity bus fares/schedules, sight hours & admission prices, and Lo de Silverio's posted hours. Re-check before travel: the USD/UYU exchange rate (moves week to week), the exact 2027 Desfile de Llamadas parade dates (Montevideo's official event page had not posted them as of this check — see the Plan tab), the US State Department advisory level (its page blocks automated fetches; needs a manual check before publish), Lo de Silverio's tasting/menu pricing (not listed online), El Palenque's opening hours (its own site posts none), the February 2027 Palacio Salvo tour listing (Red Ticket posts one month at a time), and the Laguna Garzón operator (its site is unreachable).

entry.visa: Visa-free for tourism, up to 90 days
entry.passportValidity: No fixed minimum stated by Uruguay's own rules, but carry at least 6 months' validity — standard airline/onward-travel practice
entry.note: A US passport holder traveling on a regular (non-diplomatic/official) passport needs no visa for a tourist stay. Diplomatic, official, and service passports do require one — irrelevant for a regular tourist trip.

items.note: Rioplatense 'vos' form (not 'tú') — standard here, not informal-only.
